newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom plans to start U.S. services.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom plans to start U.S. services.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd said it will apply to provide telecom services in the U.S. later this week when the nation opens its market under a new World Trade Organisation (WTO) agreement.

"We will apply certain services as soon as the U.S. invitation starts later this week," a spokeswoman told Reuters on Wednesday. She said the company has not yet finalised which services to apply for but applications would likely be for fax and data services.
The telecom giant is expected to apply for offering international fax and data services to big companies through private networks.

Under the WTO telecom pact agreed at mid-February, 68 countries agreed to open the global telecoms market following three years of negotiations. The pact on basic telecoms would bring services such as satellite systemes, cellular phones, data transmission and paging under the WTO's umbrella.
Hong Kong has committed to open its market to callback and international simple resale of fax and data services.
Hong Kong Telecom said earlier that it planned to apply for licences to provide virtual private network and international simple resale services in the U.S. and other countries.
